claims.text: A conformal graphene coating can be applied to tungsten particles before copper infiltration.
The graphene interlayer can form a well-bonded engineered interface between tungsten and copper.
The graphene interlayer facilitates improved phonon coupling across the W–Cu interface.
The graphene interlayer facilitates improved electron coupling across the W–Cu interface.
Graphene has extremely high in-plane thermal conductivity.
A graphene nanolayer at the W–Cu interface reduces thermal boundary resistance.
Reduced W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance provides a more efficient pathway for heat transfer.
Graphene's intrinsic strength and chemical stability help maintain robust interfacial bonding in W–Cu composites.
The graphene interlayer mitigates stress concentrations at the W–Cu interface.
Graphene-coated W–Cu composites will have higher overall thermal conductivity than otherwise identical uncoated W–Cu composites.
Graphene-coated W–Cu composites will retain mechanical properties at least equivalent to those of otherwise identical uncoated composites.
Graphene-coated W–Cu composites will retain irradiation resistance at least equivalent to that of otherwise identical uncoated composites.
The predicted benefits should persist at elevated temperatures and under moderate neutron irradiation representative of fusion-reactor environments.
The predicted benefits depend on the graphene coating retaining its integrity under relevant operating temperatures and irradiation doses.
Interfacial degradation or delamination would limit the thermal and durability benefits of the graphene interlayer.
